alternatives_considered.approach: Throw redirect('/?left=...') from leaveGroup after the commit
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Breaks the typed MemberResult contract every client and test relies on, and the codebase documents navigation as the client's job because a redirect thrown from an action unwinds its transaction (src/app/actions/groups.ts:21, src/components/join-screen.tsx:24-25).

alternatives_considered.approach: Keep rendering the members screen after a leave instead of notFound so LeaveButton stays mounted
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: TR-1 requires a non-member to get the not-found page rather than a list that confirms the group exists.

alternatives_considered.approach: Serializable transactions or an advisory lock around joinGroupIfAbsent
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING is the native idempotent write and keeps the existing empty-RETURNING no-op path that joinWithToken already handles.

work_order.approach: Two minimal fixes, one per finding, neither changing a contract. (1) In joinGroupIfAbsent (src/lib/access.ts:526-534), append 'ON CONFLICT (group_id, user_id) WHERE user_id IS NOT NULL AND removed_at IS NULL DO NOTHING' between the WHERE NOT EXISTS select and RETURNING, keeping the existing empty-RETURNING-means-no-op mapping. The WHERE NOT EXISTS stays as the fast path; the ON CONFLICT clause is the backstop that turns the loser's unique violation under READ COMMITTED overlap into the same graceful no-op PGlite already proves. joinWithToken needs no change: it only writes member.joined when a memberId came back and returns the group id either way, so both racers answer ok:true with exactly one row and one feed entry. (2) In useMemberAction (src/components/member-actions.tsx:18-37), move the onSuccess call out of the useEffect-on-state and into the awaited action continuation: wrap the action so the resolved MemberResult is passed to onSuccessRef before being returned to useActionState, and delete the state effect. An unmount (the revalidatePath in leaveGroup re-rendering the members page to notFound) discards the state update and the effect with it, but it cannot cancel the pending promise continuation, so router.push('/?left=...') now survives exactly the commit that used to take it with the component. This is the same bug class src/components/join-screen.tsx:14-20 documents, fixed the only way TR-1 allows here: the page must notFound for a non-member, so the navigation must not depend on staying mounted. RemoveButton's noop onSuccess, the typed results, and the revalidatePath calls are all untouched.
assumptions: Neon runs the default READ COMMITTED isolation, which is what makes the overlapping-pair violation possible.
PGlite matches Postgres ON CONFLICT and partial-index predicate semantics, so the new duplicate-insert case proves the conflict target matches.
LeaveButton is only rendered on the members page (src/components/members-screen.tsx:75-77); no other screen depends on its navigation.
work_order.confidence_rationale: Both root causes read verbatim in the current code and both fixes follow precedents this repo already documents (join-screen unmount note, navigation-is-the-client's-job rule); the only thing CI cannot prove is a truly overlapping pair of transactions on Neon.

qa_script: Boot the app (npm run sdlc:serve) and sign up an owner; create a group named Lisbon.
Copy the invite link; sign up a second user, open the link and confirm twice: second confirm shows the already-in state with a working Open link and no error.
As the member, open the members page, click Leave, confirm: expect navigation to /?left=<id> with the 'You left Lisbon · Undo' notice.
Click Undo within ten seconds: the notice clears and Lisbon returns to the list.
As the owner, remove a member from the members page: the row disappears and the page stays put with no navigation.
Reload home after eleven seconds with ?left= still in the URL: no notice renders.
risks: The ON CONFLICT predicate must match the partial unique index exactly or Postgres raises at runtime instead of doing nothing; the new duplicate-insert integration case runs the same semantics on PGlite and fails loudly on a mismatch.
A truly overlapping pair of join transactions cannot be staged on PGlite or in CI; the Neon overlap is proven by inspection, and a preview pointed at a Neon branch is the only live proof.
useMemberAction is shared with RemoveButton; its onSuccess is a noop so in-place removal behavior is unchanged, guarded by the new component case asserting no navigation.
work_order.root_cause: Two unrelated defects filed as one ticket. (1) joinGroupIfAbsent writes INSERT..SELECT..WHERE NOT EXISTS with a bare RETURNING; under READ COMMITTED two overlapping same-user joins both pass NOT EXISTS and the loser raises a unique violation on members_group_user_active_idx instead of taking the no-op path, which surfaces as a 500 on Neon. PGlite serializes statements so the existing racing-confirms test cannot show it. (2) LeaveButton navigates via a useEffect on the action result, but leaveGroup's revalidatePath re-renders the members page to notFound (the caller is no longer a member), unmounting LeaveButton in the same commit that delivers the result — the effect never runs and the user strands on 'This group isn't available' with the Undo notice unreachable. Severity reassessed from QA's minor to moderate: the membership write is correct and nothing is lost, but the only Undo affordance for a reversible action is unreachable from the members page, which is where a member leaves.

cases: A duplicate join insert carrying the new ON CONFLICT predicate against an existing active membership returns zero rows and raises nothing, proving the conflict target matches members_group_user_active_idx (a mismatched predicate raises instead of returning empty).
The existing sequential double-confirm no-op case and the racing-confirms ok/ok case keep passing unchanged with one row and one member.joined entry.
Leave confirmed and the component unmounted before the action resolves still pushes /?left=<groupId> to the router; this fails on the old effect-based navigation and passes on the continuation.
A refused leave (ok:false with a formError) pushes nothing and renders the sentence in place.
A successful removal pushes nothing and stays on the page, guarding the shared hook's other caller.

work_order.understanding: Follow-ups from #5/PR #22, one ticket for two unrelated defects: (1) concurrent same-user group joins can 500 on Neon because joinGroupIfAbsent relies on INSERT..WHERE NOT EXISTS without ON CONFLICT, so the loser of a truly overlapping pair hits the partial unique index instead of the graceful no-op; (2) leaving a group from the members page strands the member on the not-found members page instead of home with the 'You left <group> · Undo' notice, because revalidatePath unmounts LeaveButton before its state.ok effect can navigate. Both reproduce in the code as it stands; neither was fixed by a later round.
unknowns: Whether QA can stage two truly overlapping join transactions against a Neon-backed preview to prove the race end-to-end.
